clue.text: List of biblical books held by academy

indicators.note: held by means the books sit inside the academy's abbreviation

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A list of scriptural books kept at some learned institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a roster, a list of people's turns of duty.

clue.text: Only males go in at such a meeting

indicators.note: go in tells us the other words are placed inside the little word at

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
men are males

explanation.surface: A men-only gathering where only males are admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only males' paints a men's club, but 'Only' works as the conjunction 'but'; the definition stretches 'meeting' to a point where two things join.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is a meeting of two things where they touch or join end to end.

clue.text: This was not played when we were at school

definitions.text: This was not played when we were at school

parts.words: This was not played when we were at school
parts.note: the idiom is 'to play' this, meaning to skip lessons; the virtuous were never guilty of it

explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil absent without leave; the idiom for skipping school uses the verb play.

clue.text: A tyrant will appear the day Riot Act is reformed

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for day

indicators.note: is reformed says the letters of the riot act are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A despot will emerge on the day public-order law is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to disperse unruly crowds; 'is reformed' is the anagram signal, while 'will appear' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is an absolute ruler, which is what a tyrant is.

clue.text: Swallow or dove circling over ancient city

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the second
circling suggests the letters of dove are going round and so jumbled

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Two birds, a swallow and a dove, flying around above an old ruined city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird beside the dove but is the verb to gulp down; 'over' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to eat greedily, to gulp down or swallow.

clue.text: A bit of an eye for a girl

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring round the pupil
a girl's name, also of a flower

explanation.definitionFit: Iris is both the pigmented part of the eye and a common girl's name.

clue.text: Refrained from supporting a tedious man

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
a bore is a tiresome person

explanation.surface: Someone declined to back a dull fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbore is the past tense of forbear, to hold back or abstain.

clue.text: Gun company occupied by receiver

indicators.note: occupied by means the firm has another word living inside it

parts.note: a firm is a business company
the ear receives sound

explanation.surface: An arms firm taken over by an official receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' suggests a bankruptcy official, but it is the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is any gun, such as a rifle or pistol.

clue.text: Company project

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play collectively
to throw or fling, as a fishing line

explanation.definitionFit: Cast is the whole troupe of performers in a show, and also means to throw forward.

clue.text: Ship's follower hung about an old sailor

definitions.meaning: a seabird known for trailing vessels across the ocean
the bird shot in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner and then hung round his neck

explanation.definitionFit: This great seabird follows ships, and in Coleridge's poem one was hung round the mariner's neck as a burden.

clue.text: Top military reportedly outlawed musicians

parts.note: the brass, or top brass, are high-ranking officers

indicators.note: reportedly means the next word is what we hear, spelt differently

parts.note: outlawed means banned

explanation.surface: Senior officers have, it is said, been prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is a group of musicians playing brass instruments.

clue.text: Get an order for the middleman

indicators.note: order means the letters of get an are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Place an order through a go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of others, a go-between or intermediary.

clue.text: Last word to the French about to expire

indicators.note: about means the French phrase goes around the other piece

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
to die is to expire

explanation.surface: A dying person's final words, spoken in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the French' looks like the farewell's addressees, but it is AU, which goes 'about' DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu, meaning farewell, is a parting word, the final thing said before leaving.

clue.text: Rates ski resort as "one star"

indicators.note: read as re-sort: the letters of rates ski are sorted again

explanation.surface: A guidebook giving a ski resort a lowly one-star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday destination but reads as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the printed symbol shaped like a little star.

clue.text: Stories that may be written down — or up

indicators.text: that may be written down — or up
indicators.note: in a down answer, the word reads the same whether you go down the grid or up it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Tales that can be recorded on paper, one way or another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long narrative tales, originally Norse heroic stories.

clue.text: Carefully analyse Kipling's work, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is street, a way
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: Studying Kipling's writing closely, in a particular manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift is to examine closely and sort through, separating good from bad.

clue.text: It gives height in flight

parts.note: not aviation: a flight of stairs, where each vertical board lifts you a step

explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of a stair step, adding height to a staircase.

clue.text: Sailor climbs ropes — these?

parts.note: the small cords tied across a ship's shrouds forming steps that seamen climb aloft

explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the rope rungs fixed across the shrouds that crew climb to go aloft.

clue.text: Pound in silver received in church

indicators.note: received in means the metal goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Money and silver handed over at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money, with silver, but is an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for stray animals, and a cage confines animals likewise.

clue.text: Collected and wrote notes

explanation.definitionFit: Composed means calm and unruffled, and also having written a musical work.

clue.text: Bizarre article about posh operatic lady

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the next piece
bizarre means strange, so the letters of article are made strange by jumbling

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A strange piece of writing about some upper-class person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' rearranges ARTICLE into LCRETIA, which goes 'about' U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rape of Lucretia is Britten's opera whose title role is a Roman noblewoman.

clue.text: Called about religious instruction, being enthusiastic

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: Phoning about RE lessons with eager keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very eager and keen.

clue.text: Gets rid of depression

definitions.meaning: low spirits, as in 'down in the ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Dumps means discards, and the dumps is a state of gloom or sadness.

clue.text: They take food off plates when rinsed off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of rinsed have gone bad and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Food comes off plates when they are washed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures washing up, but the eaters clear the plates first.
explanation.definitionFit: Diners are people eating meals, who clear their plates.

clue.text: Bond fired at random, contrary to orders

indicators.note: at random means the letters of bond fired come in no set order

explanation.surface: James Bond shooting wildly, against instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden is prohibited, against the rules or commands given.

clue.text: Give a signal and slow down

definitions.meaning: to wave a banner to signal

explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to signal with a banner, and also to weaken or slow down.

clue.text: Pained expression when top of finger is cut off

indicators.note: top of names the first letter as the one at issue
is cut off means that letter is removed

parts.note: to finger something is to touch it

explanation.surface: A cry of pain when a fingertip is sliced away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finger' looks like a noun but is the verb TOUCH, losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation people make when hurt.

clue.text: The essential point for lawbreakers, say

indicators.note: say signals that we need the spoken sound of the word

parts.note: crooks are criminals, lawbreakers

explanation.surface: The key matter, as far as criminals are concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux is the heart of a matter, its central and decisive issue.

clue.text: Artist's bow tie?

definitions.meaning: a person who paints pictures; the 's stands for is
a rope at the front of a boat used to tie it up

explanation.definitionFit: A painter is an artist, and also the mooring rope at a boat's bow.

clue.text: Helped with the dishes but forgot part

definitions.meaning: wiped the washed crockery with a cloth
of an actor, forgot the lines of their role

explanation.definitionFit: Dried up describes drying crockery after washing, and also an actor's forgetting lines.
